learningPaths.title: Advanced RAG Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level Advanced Retrieval & RAG Systems curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation architectures, including query intent routing, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) context aggregation, hybrid BM25/vector/metadata indexing, iterative Self-RAG and Corrective RAG (CRAG) loops, knowledge grounding and citation attribution, and retrieval failure modes with engineering mitigations.

learningPaths.title: AI Agents & Tool Use Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level AI Agents & Tool Use curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the conceptual foundations of AI agents and external actions, including perception-action loops, ReAct planning and task decomposition, function schema validation and tool calling, short-term vs. long-term memory configurations, self-correcting critique loops, and collaborative multi-agent patterns.

learningPaths.title: AI Representation Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to foundational representation concepts used in modern AI systems, beginning with embeddings and semantic similarity.

learningPaths.title: AI Research and Frontier Topics
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level AI Research and Frontier Topics curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to frontier AI research: scaling laws, reasoning models, MoE architectures, world models, neurosymbolic AI, and AI for scientific discovery. Focus on enduring research principles rather than specific models or benchmarks.

learningPaths.title: AI Safety and Alignment Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level AI Safety and Alignment curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to comprehensive AI safety and alignment concepts, including prompt injection attacks and defenses, jailbreak techniques and refusal bypass, grounding and verification strategies for output reliability, Constitutional AI principles and mechanisms, multi-layer guardrail architectures for production LLM systems, and policy enforcement and output validation frameworks covering structural and semantic validation, approval chains, and safe degradation strategies.

learningPaths.title: Computer Vision Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level computer vision curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the spatial, channel, and mathematical representations of digital images, convolution operations, Sobel filter feature maps, and classical vs deep learning paradigms.

learningPaths.title: Convolutional Neural Networks Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level convolutional neural network curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the architectural components, spatial downsampling methods, receptive field calculations, layered visual hierarchies, and transfer learning backbones of Convolutional Neural Networks.

learningPaths.title: Deep Learning Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level deep learning curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the core architecture, optimization, and training protocols of deep artificial neural networks, building upon mathematical representation and machine learning structures.

learningPaths.title: Fine-Tuning & Adaptation Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level Model Adaptation curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the conceptual foundations of model adaptation, including gradient updates, instruction alignment, Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT/LoRA), SFT loss masking, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), and domain specialization.

learningPaths.title: LLM Evaluation and Benchmarking
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level LLM Evaluation and Benchmarking curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to comprehensive LLM evaluation and benchmarking methodologies, including automatic evaluation metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, BERTScore), human evaluation protocols (fluency, coherence, factuality, annotation agreement), task-specific benchmarking (MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval, BIG-bench), RAG evaluation frameworks (faithfulness, context precision, context recall, answer relevance), hallucination detection and analysis (intrinsic vs. extrinsic, grounding, verifiability), and agent evaluation methodologies (planning, tool use, multi-step execution, robustness).

learningPaths.title: Large Language Model Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level Large Language Model architecture curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the conceptual foundations of Large Language Models (LLMs), including scaling laws, autoregressive sampling decoding, prompt shaping, KV caching limits, In-Context Learning activation states, and hallucination alignment mitigations.

learningPaths.title: Machine Learning Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level machine learning curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the core concepts and evaluation protocols of machine learning, mapping foundational mathematics and statistics to practical classification, regression, and optimization tasks.

learningPaths.title: Mathematical Foundations for AI
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level mathematical curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to essential mathematical concepts and structures underpinning modern artificial intelligence, machine learning, and retrieval systems, including basic tensor arrays, vector projections, and dimensional transformations.

learningPaths.title: Multimodal AI Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level Multimodal AI Foundations curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the conceptual foundations of Multimodal AI systems, including vision-language projections, shared joint latent spaces, batch contrastive learning optimizations (like CLIP), cross-attention image captioning decoders, visual question answering (VQA) multi-modal transformers, and cross-modal database search indexes.

learningPaths.title: Object Detection Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level object detection curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to classification-regression multi-task networks, coordinate box systems, Jaccard Index overlap ratios, anchor setups, non-maximum peak score suppression loops, and single-stage vs. multi-stage proposals.

learningPaths.title: Production AI Systems and MLOps
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level Production AI Systems and MLOps curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to production AI systems and MLOps, including model serving and inference optimization, monitoring and observability, data and concept drift detection, ML pipelines and orchestration, model versioning and experiment tracking, and deployment strategies with rollback mechanisms.

learningPaths.title: Segmentation Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level image segmentation curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to image segmentation paradigms, including category-level pixel grouping, output logit classification heads, one-hot map formats, encoder-decoder bottlenecks, skip connection spatial restores, and U-Net vs. Mask R-CNN architectural distinctions.

learningPaths.title: Statistics and Probability for AI
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level statistical curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to key probability structures and statistical reasoning methods used in AI engineering, machine learning optimization, and experimental analysis.

learningPaths.title: Transformer Foundations
learningPaths.overview: This Learning Path organizes multiple Modules into a coherent, high-level Transformer architecture curriculum progression.
learningPaths.aim: Introduce learners to the conceptual foundations of the Transformer architecture, including attention parallelization, scaled Query-Key-Value operations, multi-head attention subspaces, sinusoidal positional encoding, encoder/decoder causal masking, and subword tokenization representations.

learningPaths.title: Convolution in Computer Vision
learningPaths.overview: From classical image kernels to learned CNN feature maps. Covers 2D discrete convolution, cross-correlation, parameters, classical filters, and the transition to learned convolutional filters.
learningPaths.aim: Understand convolution as the foundational local operation in computer vision and relate fixed hand-designed filters to learned CNN filters.

modules.title: Advanced Retrieval Pipelines
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to advanced query and context engineering within retrieval pipelines, focusing on query intent-based routing switches, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) rank-combining math, and multi-index hybrid search architectures.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to advanced query and context engineering within retrieval pipelines, focusing on query intent-based routing switches, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) rank-combining math, and multi-index hybrid search architectures.

modules.title: Agent Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to perception-action loops, goal-directed planning, task decomposition frameworks (like ReAct), and the structured schemas and execution logic of tool calling and API interaction.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the architectural core of AI agents, focusing on perception-action loops, goal-directed planning, task decomposition frameworks (like ReAct), and the structured schemas and execution logic of tool calling and API interaction.

modules.title: Agent Memory & Orchestration
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to agent memory and orchestration patterns, focusing on the differences between active context short-term memory and long-term vector database storage, critique-based self-correction loops for error recovery, and collaborative multi-agent patterns using specialized personas and message routing.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to agent memory and orchestration patterns, focusing on the differences between active context short-term memory and long-term vector database storage, critique-based self-correction loops for error recovery, and collaborative multi-agent patterns using specialized personas and message routing.

modules.title: Agentic Retrieval Systems
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to loop-based agentic retrieval architectures, focusing on Self-RAG and Corrective RAG (CRAG) iteration patterns, knowledge grounding and factual citation attribution, and the taxonomy of retrieval failure modes with their corresponding engineering mitigations.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to loop-based agentic retrieval architectures, focusing on Self-RAG and Corrective RAG (CRAG) iteration patterns, knowledge grounding and factual citation attribution, and the taxonomy of retrieval failure modes with their corresponding engineering mitigations.

modules.title: AI Safety Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering the foundational concepts of AI safety as applied to LLM systems, focusing on prompt injection attacks and defenses, jailbreak techniques and refusal bypass, and grounding and verification strategies for ensuring response reliability.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to core AI safety concepts for LLMs, including the distinction between prompt injection and jailbreak attacks, layered defense strategies, and operational grounding and verification techniques for improving output reliability.

modules.title: Alignment and Guardrails
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering behavioral alignment and operational guardrails for LLM systems, focusing on Constitutional AI principles and self-critique mechanisms, multi-layer guardrail architectures for production systems, and policy enforcement and output validation frameworks.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to alignment and guardrail approaches for LLMs, including constitutional principles for model behavior, layered guardrail architectures covering input to post-processing, and comprehensive policy enforcement and output validation strategies.

modules.title: Alignment & Specialization
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to target-only cross-entropy loss masking in Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), human preference reward modeling, policy optimizations (PPO / KL penalties), medical/financial/legal domain pre-training, and Fine-Tuning vs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectural trade-offs.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to model alignment and specialization techniques, including target-only cross-entropy loss masking in Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), human preference reward modeling, policy optimizations (PPO / KL penalties), medical/financial/legal domain pre-training, and Fine-Tuning vs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectural trade-offs.

modules.title: CNN Building Blocks
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to Convolutional Neural Network topologies, downsampling layers, and spatial layout calculators.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the core building blocks of Convolutional Neural Networks, including weight sharing, local connectivity, spatial max/average pooling downsamplings, and stride/padding output layout calculations.

modules.title: Core Machine Learning Concepts
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to learning paradigms and optimization feedback loops.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the core paradigms of machine learning, including supervised learning (classification and regression), unsupervised learning (clustering and dimensionality reduction), and loss functions.

modules.title: Detection Architectures
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to anchor priors, box selection heuristics, and multi-stage extraction workflows.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the architectural paradigms of object detection, including anchor-based templates vs. anchor-free center coordinate regressions, Non-Maximum Suppression overlap suppressions, and one-stage vs. two-stage candidate proposal pipelines.

modules.title: Detection Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to classification-regression task splits, pixel coordinate maps, and box overlap areas.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the fundamentals of object detection, including spatial localization vs. classification heads, absolute and normalized bounding box coordinate representations, and overlap calculation metrics (Intersection over Union).

modules.title: Frontier AI Paradigms
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering frontier AI research paradigms: world models and latent simulation, neurosymbolic AI, and AI for scientific discovery.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to emerging AI research paradigms, including world models and latent simulation for planning and reasoning, neurosymbolic AI bridging neural learning with symbolic reasoning, and AI-driven scientific discovery for hypothesis generation, surrogate simulation, and automated experimentation.

modules.title: Frontier Model Scaling
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering frontier model scaling, including scaling laws and emergent behavior, reasoning models and test-time compute, and mixture-of-experts architectures.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to frontier research in model scaling, including scaling laws relating parameters, data, and compute to model capabilities, reasoning models that allocate additional computation during inference, and mixture-of-experts architectures that decouple parameter count from computational cost.

modules.title: Image Representation Foundations
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to spatial image layouts, tensor channel groupings, and resizing interpolations.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to computational representations of digital images, including pixel coordinates, intensity grids, channel tensors, color spaces, and resolution downsampling/resizing interpolations.

modules.title: Linear Algebra Foundations
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to numerical arrays, dot product mappings, and parallel row-column multiplications.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the basic structures and operations of linear algebra underpinning modern artificial intelligence, including scalars, vectors, matrices, tensors, dot products, and matrix multiplication.

modules.title: LLM Context & Behavior
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to context sizes, activation state dynamics, and factual reliability mappings.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the behavioral properties of LLMs during inference, including context window constraints, Key-Value (KV) cache sizing, In-Context Learning (ICL) activation theories, and the causes and mitigation strategies for hallucinations.

modules.title: LLM Core Concepts
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to Large Language Model scaling laws, token-by-token decoding generation, and prompt block layouts.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the architectural core of Large Language Models (LLMs), including self-supervised pre-training, Kaplan and Chinchilla scaling laws, token-by-token autoregressive generation loops, temperature/top-k/top-p decoding parameter controls, and prompt shaping mechanics.

modules.title: LLM Evaluation Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering the foundational concepts of LLM evaluation, focusing on automatic evaluation metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, BERTScore), human evaluation protocols (fluency, coherence, factuality, inter-annotator agreement), and task-specific benchmarking methodologies (general vs. specialized benchmarks, statistical interpretation).
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the core evaluation paradigms for LLMs, including automatic metric computation and limitations, human annotation design and agreement measurement, and benchmark selection and result interpretation.

modules.title: Mathematical Representations
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to angular vectors normalization, coordinate grid transformations, and data projections.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to mathematical representations and mappings used in AI, including normalized cosine similarity metrics, geometric linear transformations, and high-dimensional reduction methods (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP).

modules.title: MLOps Lifecycle
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering the MLOps lifecycle, focusing on ML pipelines and workflow orchestration, model versioning and experiment tracking for reproducibility, and deployment strategies with rollback mechanisms for safe production releases.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the MLOps lifecycle, including ML pipeline design and workflow orchestration, model versioning and experiment tracking for reproducibility, and deployment strategies with rollback mechanisms for safe production releases.

modules.title: Model Adaptation Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to weight adjustments, learning rate schedules, catastrophic forgetting risks, instruction tuning alignments, and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) low-rank factorization (LoRA) mathematics.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the foundations of adapting pre-trained Large Language Models (LLMs), including weight adjustments, learning rate schedules, catastrophic forgetting risks, instruction tuning alignments, and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) low-rank factorization (LoRA) mathematics.

modules.title: Model Generalization and Evaluation
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to validation split protocols, model complexity limitations, and mathematical error components.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to principles of model evaluation and generalization limits in AI, including train/validation/test splits, overfitting, underfitting, and the bias-variance tradeoff.

modules.title: Multimodal Applications
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to downstream applications of multimodal architectures, focusing on encoder-decoder autoregressive image captioning, multimodal Transformer question-answering (VQA), and text-to-image/image-to-text cross-modal vector database search.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to downstream applications of multimodal architectures, focusing on encoder-decoder autoregressive image captioning, multimodal Transformer question-answering (VQA), and text-to-image/image-to-text cross-modal vector database search.

modules.title: Multimodal Representations
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to representing multiple modalities (like vision and language) in a joint latent space, including vision-language linear projection mapping, cross-modal embedding cosine similarities, and batch contrastive learning InfoNCE optimization.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the core mathematical and architectural concepts behind representing multiple modalities (like vision and language) in a joint latent space, including vision-language linear projection mapping, cross-modal embedding cosine similarities, and batch contrastive learning InfoNCE optimization.

modules.title: Neural Network Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to deep neural network structure, propagation, and activations.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the architectural fundamentals of deep artificial neural networks, including layer typologies, forward propagation flows, and activation functions.

modules.title: Optimization and Training
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to backpropagation calculus, optimization algorithms, and scheduling parameters.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to deep learning optimization, including backpropagation algorithms, SGD and Adam optimizers, and training schedules (epochs, batches, and learning rates).

modules.title: Probability Foundations
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to random variables mapping, distribution curves, and Bayesian conditional probability updates.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the basic principles of probability that support modern artificial intelligence, including random variables, probability distributions, and belief updating via Bayes' Theorem.

modules.title: Production AI Systems
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering production AI systems concepts, including model serving architectures and inference optimization, monitoring and observability for deployed models, and drift detection for maintaining model performance over time.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to production AI systems concepts, including model serving architectures and inference optimization, monitoring and observability for deployed models, and drift detection for maintaining model performance over time.

modules.title: RAG & Agent Evaluation
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons covering evaluation frameworks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation and AI agent systems, focusing on RAG evaluation dimensions (faithfulness, context precision, context recall, answer relevance), hallucination detection and analysis (intrinsic vs. extrinsic, grounding, verifiability), and agent evaluation methodologies (planning, tool use, multi-step execution, robustness).
modules.aim: Introduce learners to evaluation methodologies for RAG pipelines and AI agents, including RAG-specific quality metrics inspired by RAGAS, hallucination classification and detection approaches, and agent evaluation dimensions covering planning, tool use, and execution reliability.

modules.title: Representation Learning in CNNs
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to hierarchical spatial context sizes, Gabor-to-semantic filter abstractions, and backbone model parameter transfers.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to spatial representation learning inside deep CNNs, including receptive field growth hierarchies, Gabor-to-semantic feature transitions, and pretrained weight transfers (feature extractors vs. fine-tuning).

modules.title: Retrieval Optimization Techniques
modules.overview: This module organizes multiple lessons related to search ranking fusion, cross-attention scoring models, and LLM context window optimization techniques.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to techniques for optimizing search results and context windows, including lexical-semantic hybrid search, neural cross-encoder reranking, and context window layout management.

modules.title: Retrieval Pipeline Foundations
modules.overview: This module organizes multiple lessons related to initial data ingestion, representation, and query pre-processing stages of modern retrieval pipelines.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the first stages of modern retrieval pipelines: splitting unstructured documents, selecting suitable embedding models, and preprocessing raw user queries.

modules.title: Segmentation Architectures
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to instance masks, spatial bottlenecks, and encoder-decoder topologies.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to segmentation architectures, including instance isolation masks, encoder-decoder spatial bottlenecks, skip connection edge restorations, and U-Net vs. Mask R-CNN paradigm comparisons.

modules.title: Segmentation Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to pixel classification, channel vectors, and lookup maps.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the fundamentals of image segmentation, including semantic category grouping, pixel-wise classification logs, output logit channel Softmax activations, and integer label map annotations.

modules.title: Semantic Representations Foundations
modules.overview: This module organizes multiple lessons into a coherent, high-level learning unit focusing on semantic representations.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to semantic representations and meaning-oriented comparison as foundations for retrieval, recommendation, clustering, and LLM systems.

modules.title: Sequence Representation
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to positional vectors, causal masks, and vocabulary representations.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to sequence representations in Transformers, including absolute/relative positional encodings, sinusoidal wave addition layers, encoder vs. decoder causal mask routing, and subword tokenization dictionary lookups.

modules.title: Statistical Reasoning for AI
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to statistical expectation values, dispersion bounds, data selection biases, and correlation limitations.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to essential statistical reasoning principles in AI, including expected values, variance metrics, bias-variance tradeoffs, representative sampling, data drift, and correlation vs. causation.

modules.title: Transformer Fundamentals
modules.overview: This module organizes foundational lessons related to Transformer parallel pipelines, Query-Key-Value scores, and subspace dimensions.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to the architectural core of the Transformer model, including parallel processing features, scaled Query/Key/Value self-attention functions, and multi-head representation subspace concatenations.

modules.title: Vector Retrieval Architectures
modules.overview: This module organizes multiple lessons related to vector storage systems and downstream retrieval augmentation workflows into a single coherent learning unit.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to vector storage engines, indexing strategies, metadata filtering, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) loops as modern AI retrieval systems.

modules.title: Visual Feature Extraction Foundations
modules.overview: This module organizes lessons related to 2D image matrix filtering operations, feature maps, and computer vision paradigms.
modules.aim: Introduce learners to spatial feature extraction in computer vision, including 2D convolutions (kernels, stride, padding), feature maps (gradients, blurring), and the paradigm shift from classical hand-crafted descriptors to deep representation learning.

modules.title: Convolution: Spatial-Domain Filtering
modules.overview: Module covering 2D convolution, cross-correlation, kernel parameters, classical filters, and the bridge to learned CNN filters.
modules.aim: Master the local operation that underpins all CNN feature extraction.
